calls.headline: Inflation eases to 12% as Egypt's real yield widens to about 14 points
calls.body: Annual headline inflation slowed to 12.0% in October from 12.8%, with prices up 0.6% on the month, CAPMAS said (Amwal Al Ghad); urban inflation, the central bank's target measure, was reported at 12.7% from 13.9% (Rio Times, not yet confirmed by the central bank). The overnight deposit rate is 20% after November's 100 basis point rise, and Thursday's 364-day bill cleared at 26.03%. National Bank of Egypt and Banque Misr raise their main fixed certificates by a point to 18.75% from Sunday (Youm7). The central bank's dollar rate ended the week at EGP 54.01, a sixth straight fall and 3.8% lower in November.
calls.view: Falling inflation under unchanged rates is the best case for the carry trade: foreign holders of bills now earn about 14 points over inflation, which supports the pound toward EGP 53–54.5 and keeps December 17 a likely hold. Banks gain most: high asset yields and still-cheap current accounts, with CIB's results on Wednesday the test. Banks lifting fixed rates shows they expect rates to stay high for a while.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 56 before the end of November, or Sunday's and Thursday's auctions clear well below last week's yields as foreign demand fades.

calls.headline: Wall Street steadies, but a hot US jobs report lifts the dollar
calls.line: Sunday's reopening faces a calmer Nasdaq but a dollar near its 52-week high and rising Fed hike odds.
calls.body: The Nasdaq rose 1.09% and the S&P 500 0.31% on Friday after Thursday's 4.4% fall, though the S&P 500 still lost 2.7% on the week. US employers added 165,000 jobs in October against forecasts near 65,000–70,000 and unemployment fell to 4.1% (BLS). The dollar index rose 0.7% to 102.28, within 0.3% of its 52-week high, and the 10-year Treasury yield to 4.86%. Traders priced about a 77–80% chance of a Fed hike on December 9, per CME FedWatch as reported by The Rio Times and Coinpaper.
calls.view: Thursday's risk-off fear, the reason foreign money might sell Egyptian stocks on Sunday, eased on Friday; the new pressure is US rates. A 25 basis point Fed hike barely dents a 26% bill, so the pound's carry holds, but a stronger dollar slows the flows that lifted the pound six sessions running. Expect a flat-to-firm open led by banks.
calls.wrong: Foreign investors are net sellers on Sunday and the EGX30 closes below 50,500.

calls.headline: Banque du Caire's EGP 36bn sale tops the EGX's weekly turnover
calls.line: The state's 45% offering cleared 27 times on retail demand and trades above its price, a good sign for the next listings.
calls.body: The sale of 45% of Banque du Caire, raised from 30% on investor demand, brought in EGP 36bn; the institutional tranche was covered 7 times and the retail tranche 27 times, said Hisham El Sayed, who runs the cabinet's state-owned companies unit (Osoul Misr). The bank was the most traded stock of the week at EGP 3.49bn and closed at EGP 5.58, up 5.3% on the week and 5.3% above the EGP 5.30 offer price; CIB came second at EGP 2.47bn (Youm7). The EBRD, the IFC and foreign investment banks took part.
calls.view: A sale this size absorbed without draining the market, and trading above its price, strengthens the case for more state listings that the IMF program requires, and adds fees and trading for brokers. The stock's 30-day buy-back at the offer price for retail buyers limits the downside for now.
calls.wrong: Banque du Caire closes below EGP 5.10, about 4% under the offer price.

calls.headline: Juhayna raises dairy prices by up to 11% before Monday's results
calls.line: Price rises protect margins as costs climb; Monday's results show whether volumes held.
calls.body: From Sunday, Juhayna's 1 kg Bekhayro laban rises to EGP 44 from EGP 42.5 (+3.5%), its 200 ml Mix drink to EGP 15 from EGP 13.5 (+11.1%) and 200 ml Juhayna laban to EGP 15 from EGP 14 (+7.1%), citing production and operating costs (Masrawy, Al Khabar Live). Dairy and egg prices rose 2.5% in October (CAPMAS). Juhayna slipped 0.5% to EGP 23.83 on Thursday and is up 17.9% this year; its results for the quarter to September are expected Monday.
calls.view: Raising prices while overall inflation slows to 12% means real price gains, which supports margins; the risk is volume, after the pound's October slide squeezed household budgets. The results matter more than the price list.
calls.wrong: Juhayna closes below EGP 21.50, about 10% under Thursday, after its results.

calls.headline: A 165,000-job surprise revives December hike bets as chips bounce
calls.body: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, against forecasts near 65,000–70,000; September was revised up to 60,000 from 29,000, unemployment fell to 4.1% and hourly pay rose 0.4% (BLS, Pound Sterling Live). San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said further tightening is likely (CNBC). The 2-year Treasury yield rose to 4.51% and the 10-year to 4.86%, and the dollar index 0.7% to 102.28; CME FedWatch put a December 9 hike near 77–80% (The Rio Times, Coinpaper). Stocks still rose: the Nasdaq gained 1.09%, Nvidia 2.8%, Intel about 8% and Tesla 4.2%, while the S&P 500 lost 2.7% on the week.
calls.view: Friday was a relief bounce after the worst chip day since 2020, not a vote for higher rates; a hike is now the base case and Tuesday's CPI decides it. Higher yields hurt the stocks priced for the long term (growth, and defensives at 40-plus times earnings) and help banks' margins. Expect the bounce in chips to be tested before Nvidia reports on November 17.
calls.wrong: October CPI comes in well below forecasts (under 3.6%) and the 2-year yield falls below 4.30%, taking the hike off the table.

calls.headline: Microsoft retreats from rented AI capacity, hitting Oracle and the neoclouds
calls.line: The biggest buyer of rented AI capacity is rationing it, a demand risk for every company that sells it.
calls.body: Microsoft has tightened oversight of data center projects run by Nebius, IREN and Nscale, will not take an option to more than double its Nscale contract in Texas, and earlier dropped an Nscale site in Essex over grid delays, Bloomberg reported (via Reuters); Nebius fell about 14%, IREN 17% and CoreWeave 10% on Thursday. On Friday Bloomberg reported that Microsoft is ending a 2023 deal to rent AI computing capacity on older Nvidia chips from Oracle (via Cryptopolitan). Oracle fell about 4% during the day and closed at $116.01, within 0.9% of its 52-week low and 40.5% lower this year; Microsoft fell 1.0% to $530.61.
calls.view: For Microsoft this is cost discipline as it builds its own sites; for those renting out capacity it is demand risk, with Oracle the most exposed after planning a $20bn capital raise. It backs the desk's view that AI spenders and suppliers lag steadier earners.
calls.wrong: Oracle closes above $135 by the end of November.

calls.headline: Guidance sets the biggest moves: JFrog +35%, Atlassian −16%, Axon −18%
calls.line: Investors paid for raised outlooks and punished any slowdown, however good the quarter.
calls.body: JFrog jumped 35.3% after cloud revenue rose 60% and it raised its 2026 outlook to $680–682m; Ubiquiti gained 15.3% on a $1.07 EPS beat. Atlassian fell 16.2% after guiding fiscal 2027 growth to about 13.75% despite a 24% rise in quarterly revenue, Axon 18.2% after resetting its free cash flow outlook to $350–400m, and Microchip 10.0% on weak December-quarter guidance (GuruFocus, Simply Wall St, MarketBeat).
calls.view: With the market down 2.7% on the week, results that only meet forecasts are being sold; the premium goes to visible demand (cloud security, networking). That favors buying strength after reports over buying dips before them.
calls.wrong: Atlassian and Axon recover their losses by the end of November, which would make the selling positioning rather than a verdict on guidance.

calls.headline: Costco's October sales jump 12.6% while Walmart slips on rotation
calls.line: Steady earners keep reporting strong numbers, but rich valuations leave them exposed when money returns to tech.
calls.body: Costco's net sales rose 12.6% to $24.50bn in the four weeks to November 1, with comparable sales up 11.1% (7.3% without gasoline and currency) and digital sales up 22.5% (Zacks); the stock fell 1.1% to $1,053.56 and trades at about 51 times earnings. Walmart fell 1.7% to $125.52 on a rotation out of defensive stocks, with no company news (Investing.com); it trades at about 44 times earnings and reports on November 19. Berkshire Hathaway, 1.4% below its 52-week high, reports on Saturday.
calls.view: The rotation into steady earners is real in the numbers but expensive in the price; Friday showed how quickly it reverses on a tech bounce. Costco's sales justify its premium better than Walmart's.
calls.wrong: Walmart closes below $118 before its results.

view.headline: Slowing inflation and a 14-point real yield keep the dollar in EGP 53–54.5
view.body: October's 12.0% inflation against a 26.03% one-year bill pays foreign holders well to stay, and the six straight falls in the central bank's rate to EGP 54.01 show the flows arriving. Friday's US jobs report and a dollar near its 52-week high are the counterweight: they can slow the pound's gains, but a 25 basis point Fed hike barely narrows a gap this wide. Sunday's auction is the first test.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 56 before the end of November, or the bill auctions clear far below last week's yields.
